newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Ex RBA gov says rate cut could have been more.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Ex RBA gov says rate cut could have been more.

text.p: Former Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Bernie Fraser said on Tuesday he believed the central bank could have cut official interest rates by a full percentage point instead of half a point last month.
Fraser, asked in an interview on Australian Broadcasting Corp television whether he believed the cut could have been one point, replied: "Well, that's true".

"I thought at the time that with inflation pretty well under control, very much under control really, and the economy being a bit sluggish that we could have accommodated a one percent cut without any risks," he said.
Fraser declined to comment on whether he thought the RBA had been too timid or on whether it should cut rates again.
"It's not a matter of being timid ... I think it's a matter of weighing up the dual objectives of trying to sustain growth and trying to keep inflation under control," Fraser said.
The bank's board met for the last time in 1996 earlier on Tuesday but most analysts expect it to hold off on another rate cut until early 1997.
The RBA has twice cut its official cash rate this year to the current to 6.50 percent, the last time on November 6.
Fraser finished his seven-year term as RBA governor in mid September and was succeeded by deputy governor Ian Macfarlane.
